heroHeadline: Day 1093: Israel Marks Third Anniversary of October 7 Attack Amid Election Accountability Debate
heroSubtitle: The deadliest attack on Jewish people since the Holocaust — assault timeline, hostage crisis resolved January 2026, intelligence failures, and IDF response. On September 28, 2026 (Day 1088 / Ceasefire Day 354): Haaretz reported that Egyptian intelligence chief Abbas Kamel phoned Netanyahu days before October 7, 2023 to warn of a Hamas attack, and that Netanyahu asked UAE President Mohamed bin Zayed to deny a report that he had warned Netanyahu; former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar said he will sue Netanyahu over claims he withheld warnings. The reports rest on media sourcing and Netanyahu's office has disputed related claims.
footerNote: Data sourced from IDF, Israel Police, UN OCHA, Israeli government, USAID Office of Inspector General, US State Department, Reuters, AP, AFP, France 24, Haaretz, Times of Israel, Jerusalem Post, Ynet News, The Jewish Chronicle, Israel Hayom, Washington Post, Washington Free Beacon, JNS, Israel National News, i24NEWS, Al Jazeera, LBC, WSJ, ICJ, and institutional analyses. Casualty figures are official Israeli counts; Hamas-theater figures are separately noted and contested. All 251 hostages accounted for as of January 26, 2026. Ceasefire in effect since Oct 10, 2025 (Ceasefire Day 344 as of Sep 18). September 27 (Day 1087): IDF, Shin Bet and police Lahav 433 unit kill Saher Nidal Latfi Saqr, who drove the motorcycle that abducted Noa Argamani and Avinatan Or from the Nova festival on October 7, in a Nuseirat strike. September 26 (Day 1086): The Atlantic reports Egypt's intelligence chief Abbas Kamel flew to Israel 11 days before October 7 to warn officials of a looming Hamas attack and urge economic concessions to Hamas; Hanegbi denies the visit occurred and Netanyahu's office calls the report false. September 25 (Day 1085): NYT reports Netanyahu chaired an October 1, 2023 security meeting — six days before the attack — at which he argued for maintaining calm in Gaza to protect a potential Saudi normalization deal, overruling officials who wanted to strike Hamas figures directing West Bank attacks, and did not mention to Barnea, Gallant, Bar, Halevi, Hanegbi or Dermer the UAE warning he had personally received about 10 days earlier; five former senior Israeli officials say the warning never reached the security establishment's heads. September 24 (Day 1084): Netanyahu tells the UN General Assembly October 7 was 'the darkest day in Israel's history' amid a delegate walkout and an outside effigy protest; IDF probe finds the Paga Outpost ('Magen Be'eri') was unprepared for the October 7 infiltration, with 22 soldiers killed, 18 wounded and two taken hostage there; Tekuma Directorate reports the Gaza border region's population has grown to about 66,000, roughly 10% above pre-October 7 levels. September 18 (Day 1078): AFP/France 24 feature reports at least nine October 7 survivors and bereaved-family members running as election candidates across the political spectrum ahead of the October 27 vote, including Sharon Sharabi, Talik Gvili, Shira Shapira and Noam Tibon. September 17 (Day 1077): Hunter Biden tells LBC radio he believes Netanyahu knew in advance of the Hamas attack and deliberately allowed it to proceed to carry out an unspecified 'plan,' offering no evidence; also calls the Gaza war 'akin to genocide.' September 16 (Day 1076): IDF and Shin Bet say they killed Jihad Samih Mahmoud Ismail, a Hamas Nukhba commander tied to the October 7 killing of Sgt. Shaked Dahan and abduction of Capt. Omer Neutra, St.-Sgt. Oz Daniel and Sgt. Nimrod Cohen, in a September 11 Khan Yunis strike; separately, Foreign Ministry orders Israeli embassies worldwide to hold October 7 memorial events, with funding available on request, after a Haaretz inquiry found smaller missions lacked budget for commemorations. September 15 (Day 1075): Bereaved and hostage families release the 'Case 7/10' dossier at a Tel Aviv press conference, alleging 15 years of government decisions — including permitting Qatari funding into Gaza and rejecting a reported Shin Bet recommendation to kill Sinwar about a week before October 7 — enabled the massacre; family members Noam Peri and Gil Dickmann renew demands for a state commission of inquiry or Netanyahu's resignation. September 14 (Day 1074): Haaretz reports hostage and bereaved families were 'never a political monolith' and have struggled to find a unified role in opposition politics ahead of the election. No new tracker-relevant developments confirmed for September 12-13. September 11 (Day 1071): Col. (res.) Doron Hadar, IDF hostage-negotiation unit commander from 2007-Feb. 2024, says mediators warned for years before October 7 that Sinwar was considering a large-scale kidnapping operation as leverage in a prisoner deal, adding to the catalogue of pre-Oct. 7 warnings alongside the 'Jericho Wall' document and the disputed UAE-warning report. September 10 (Day 1070): IDF and Shin Bet kill Ismail Ibrahim Darwish Kandil, a Hamas Nukhba operative who infiltrated Israel on October 7 and took part in killing Nahal Brigade commander Col. Yonatan Steinberg, in a Khan Younis strike; separately, Netanyahu's legal team sends Haaretz a formal pre-suit warning letter over its September 8 UAE-warning report, giving 72 hours to retract before a libel suit; Haaretz says it stands by its reporting. September 9 (Day 1069): Netanyahu's office announces a libel suit against Haaretz and reporter Shlomi Eldar over its September 8 report that UAE President Mohammed bin Zayed warned him roughly 10 days before October 7 that Hamas was planning a major operation; Netanyahu's office says internal reviews found no record of the call, Haaretz stands by its report. September 8 (Day 1068): Haaretz reports, citing the book 'Kidnapped: 843 Days of Abandonment,' that Bin Zayed warned Netanyahu of a Sinwar-planned 'earthquake' operation about 10 days before October 7, and that Netanyahu did not brief his defense minister, IDF chief, or Shin Bet/Mossad directors on the call; opposition leaders Eisenkot, Bennett, Liberman and Golan renew demands for a state commission of inquiry. September 7 (Day 1067): Defense Minister Israel Katz says the IDF has been told to prepare an 'all-out war' against senior PA officials if a West Bank October 7-style attack looks imminent, following a Kusra-area stabbing; same day, a JCFA/Lazar Research poll finds 77% of Israelis (86% of Jewish Israelis) fear a repeat West Bank attack, and Brig. Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter submits an independent Knesset slate after refusing to merge with Smotrich's Religious Zionist Party, framing it around candidates 'who were not part of the events that led us to October 7.' September 6 (Day 1066): Israel's National Security Council warns the October 2026 third anniversary of October 7 is a 'particularly sensitive period' raising the risk of violent protests and attacks on Israelis and Jews abroad, citing Iran and its proxies as the primary threat and noting 25 Israelis/Jews killed overseas since the war began. September 5 (Day 1065): Channel 12 reports Brig. Gen. (res.) Ofer Winter warned Netanyahu days after October 7 that a Gaza ground offensive would cost 15,000 soldiers' lives — a claim Winter denies and actual losses (473) came nowhere near; same day, Michel Illouz, father of slain hostage Guy Illouz, tells the Habima Square protest a state commission of inquiry 'is not vengeance, not a tool to topple the government.' September 4 (Day 1064): IDF and Shin Bet kill Muhammad Mahmoud Marshad al-Qadi, the Hamas Nukhba commander who led the October 7 raid on the Sufa outpost and later held hostages in Rafah, in a Khan Yunis strike. September 3 (Day 1063): Netanyahu's office publishes his full October 7 morning timeline, revealing his first direct conversation with IDF Chief Halevi came at 9:55 a.m. — nearly 3.5 hours after the attack began; October Council calls the delay 'unfathomable,' Yair Golan says it is 'unfathomable that Netanyahu was not in touch with Halevi' as towns were overrun. September 2 (Day 1062): Hundreds gather in Skokie, Illinois to dedicate 'Hersh's Fridge,' a kosher community fridge and memorial mural to Nova hostage Hersh Goldberg-Polin, murdered by Hamas in Gaza; parents Jon Polin and Rachel Goldberg-Polin attend. September 1 (Day 1061): Netanyahu says defense officials 'deliberately chose not to wake him' before October 7 for fear of 'annoying Hamas,' then denies alleging 'betrayal,' calling it instead 'a failure, a great failure'; the same day, Yair Golan warns Sara Netanyahu of an $825,000 defamation suit over her Channel 14 insinuation that his early arrival at Nova indicated advance knowledge of the attack, and she threatens a NIS 1 million countersuit. August 31 (Day 1060): Women Demand Life activists protest at the PM's Residence marking two years since the 'Beautiful Six' hostages' bodies were recovered. August 30 (Day 1059): Former hostage Eli Sharabi and actress Shani Cohen announced as hosts of the third grassroots national October 7 memorial ceremony at Yarkon Park, Tel Aviv. August 28 (Day 1057): Nir Oz kibbutz chairman Tzvi Tessler says the majority of the community's ~400 pre-war residents still have not returned nearly three years after October 7, in which the kibbutz lost 69 people (about a quarter of its community) killed or in captivity — the highest per-capita toll of any single Oct. 7 site. August 27 (Day 1056): IDF strikes in Gaza's Al-Shati and Sabra areas kill Nabil Ibrahim Bass, a Hamas commander who infiltrated Israel on October 7, and PIJ observation commander Hamdi Ahmad Hamid Kahlil. August 26 (Day 1055): IDF kills Ismail Mohammed Ibrahim Barim in a Khan Younis strike — a Hamas commander who helped hold October 7 abductee Edan Alexander, plus Matan Zangauker and Avera Mengistu, hostage in a Gaza tunnel before their releases. August 27 (Day 1056): US State Department and USAID's Office of Inspector General debar former UNRWA school principal Hafez Mousa Mohammed Mousa — the first US debarment of a terrorist affiliated with a UN humanitarian agency — over October 7 Hamas communications role, and propose debarring three more former UNRWA teachers over October 7/Hamas/Islamic Jihad ties; Washington Free Beacon reporting citing the same USAID probe confirms UNRWA 'social worker' Faisal Ali Al-Naami, filmed dragging slain hostage Yonatan Samerano's body at Kibbutz Be'eri on October 7, was an active Hamas operative. Same day, IDF and Shin Bet announce the killing of Razek Sahil Suleiman Abu Shahma (former Sinwar bodyguard) and Hazem Mousa, both October 7 Re'im infiltrators. August 24 (Day 1053): IDF kills Nukhba terrorist Mohammad Abd al-Nasser Jabr Abu Asaad in a Deir al-Balah strike; October Council publishes 'Strategic Warning: Default 2026,' warning the IDF's pre-October 7 'conceptzia' containment mentality persists, Hamas continues rebuilding and testing the Yellow Line, and field observers are pressured into silence. August 25 (Day 1054): Netanyahu orders a UNRWA vocational training center in Kafr Aqab, East Jerusalem dismantled, citing employees' alleged October 7 involvement; IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir visits Gaza-border surveillance soldiers at Re'im Base, telling them 'one of the lessons of October 7 is that we must listen carefully to every female and male soldier' amid renewed complaints their warnings are being ignored. August 22 (Day 1051): Liad Baram, father of Nahal Oz soldier Neta Baram, tells ~250 Habima Square protesters the state has an 'unceasing and unforgivable debt' to investigate October 7 failures. August 21 (Day 1050): IDF announces it killed Sabahi Sami Mahmoud Shahata, a Hamas platoon commander who held Oct. 7 hostages, in an August 19 Nuseirat strike; follows an August 18 Al-Shati strike that killed four Nukhba commanders including another October 7 infiltrator. August 20 (Day 1049): IDF Military Advocate-General's Corps publishes its first war crimes report since October 7 — criminal probes opened into the Hind Rajab and Red Crescent-paramedics killings, WCK strike closed without charges. August 19 (Day 1048): Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara tells the High Court she backs delaying the October 7 commission-of-inquiry decision until after the October 27 election; Movement for Quality Government and the October Council reject the delay. August 18 (Day 1046): IDF confirms an August 16 strike killed Tareq Anwar Khamis Ra'i, an Islamic Jihad commander who abducted a Be'eri resident on October 7. August 13 (Day 1041): Eyal Eshel, father of slain Nahal Oz lookout Roni Eshel, tells KAN News that witnesses reported some October 7 terrorists speaking Farsi at the Nahal Oz base, reinforcing Iranian-proxy-involvement assessments. August 11 (Day 1039): Tel Aviv Municipality formally renames the Tel Aviv Museum plaza 'Hostages Square.' August 6 (Day 1034): Nissim Louk, father of Nova victim Shani Louk, confronts Transportation Minister Miri Regev at a Likud campaign stop in Jerusalem — 'You caused October 7!' August 5 (Day 1033): IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir tours Gaza, vows the military will bring every October 7 perpetrator to justice. August 8 (Day 1037): Chen family rally at Habima Square, urging voters to back only parties pledging a state commission of inquiry. July 22 (Day 1020): Government tells High Court it will not complete October 7 probe legislation before the October 27 election; October Council calls it 'contempt for the court, the rule of law, and the Israeli public.' July 17 (Day 1015): Knesset dissolves for the October 27 election in a final legislative blitz that leaves the Kallner inquiry bill unfinished. July 5 (Day 1003): Netanyahu's Cabinet defies a High Court ruling for the first time in Israeli history; Knesset Speaker Ohana refuses the court-ordered state comptroller revote — Israel has had no sitting comptroller since. July 2 (Day 1000): 1,000 days since October 7 marked with nationwide protests; High Court voids Rabello's comptroller election. October 7 Perpetrators Eliminated: Sinwar (Oct 16, 2024), Shambari (Apr 29, 2026), Haddad (May 16, 2026), Odeh (May 27, 2026), Khamis Ra'i (Aug 16, 2026), Shahata (Aug 19, 2026), al-Qadi (Sep 4, 2026), Kandil (Sep 10, 2026), Saqr (Sep 27, 2026). Last survivor: Imad Aqel (NILI target, Qassam command vacant 13+ weeks). Accountability: Kallner bill stalled after first reading; no probe before Oct 27 election; Attorney General backs delay until post-election; first IDF war crimes report opens criminal probes into Hind Rajab and Red Crescent cases; October Council warns pre-Oct 7 conceptzia persists; USAID OIG debarment track adds independent evidentiary weight to UNRWA October 7 allegations; Beyachad pledges Day-1 state commission.
